review.note: M52: this record was named "Russia (Soviet Union)" and was one record for three polities. It now carries the post-Soviet period alone, from 1991-12-21, which is where CShapes’ own first post-Soviet period begins and is not a founding. Its inception is an open question: Q159’s preferred P571 is 1263, and its other values are 880, 1125 and 1991-12-25 — one day before the Soviet Union’s dissolution. See docs/m52-russia.md §2.4.

summary: Approximately 17,075,400 km² and about 146.1 million people (2025), from Wikidata's Q159 (P2046, P1082). The English Wikipedia article "Russia", at revision 1375974488, opens: "Russia, or the Russian Federation, is a country in Eastern Europe and North Asia. It is the largest country in the world, spanning eleven time zones and sharing land borders with fourteen countries. With a population of over 140 million, Russia is the most populous country in Europe and the ninth-most populous in the world." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Entity 365 in the Gleditsch–Ward state list, as mapped by CShapes 2.0, a dataset of the borders and capitals of states and dependencies between 1886 and 2019. The dataset gives entity 365 twenty-four periods of territorial validity under one label, "Russia (Soviet Union)", which covers three polities; M52 gave the first three to `russian-empire` and the next nineteen to `soviet-union`, and this record holds the last two, from 1991-12-21. Its last capital in the dataset is Moscow. It begins on that day because that is where CShapes’ own first post-Soviet period begins, and not because any source here says a state was founded then: what this record’s inception is stays an open question, and docs/m52-russia.md says what a person has to decide.
